ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and senior officers against the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) PEP database, the UN Security Council Sanctions List (implemented under the United Nations Act 1946), the New Zealand Sanctions Regimes (including the Russia Sanctions Act 2022 and other autonomous sanctions), and the publicly issued OFAC and other allied sanctions lists as supplementary best-practice. Red-flag triggers require enhanced due diligence, adverse-media review, source-of-funds/source-of-wealth verification, and filing of a suspicious activity report (SAR) with the New Zealand FIU where warranted.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office Online Name Approval and Company Registration Portal (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Proposed company names must be submitted using standard Latin alphabetic characters; Te Reo Māori names are accepted with correct macrons/diacritics. No alternate transliteration or unofficial translation may be relied upon for registration. Names must be in English or Te Reo Māori, must comply with the Business Names Registration process, and must not create confusion with an existing registered name, including under the Identical or Similar Existing Name test.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name application is rejected, the applicant shall immediately receive a statement of reasons from the Companies Office. Within 10 working days of rejection, the applicant may file a written request for internal reconsideration to the Registrar of Companies, attaching evidence of prior use, consent from the relevant regulatory body if the name contains a restricted token, and legal arguments showing the name is not misleading or confusing. Where internal reconsideration is unsuccessful, an appeal may be filed with the High Court of New Zealand within 20 working days of the reconsideration decision. A rejected name may not be re-filed in the same or substantially similar form except with new distinguishing features. The applicant may alternatively reserve an amended name for a further 20 working day period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office address is permissible for registered office purposes in New Zealand, provided it is a real physical location where documents can be served during ordinary business hours and is not merely a postal box; for a non-licensed, low-risk digital short-drama streaming enterprise, the use of an agent's virtual office is deemed acceptable and administratively practical.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low but non-zero; estimated unannounced on-site inspection probability is less than 5% per annum for a non-licensed content distributor with no physical inventory, no cash handling, and no regulated financial activities. Additional inspection risk may arise from filter-based sanctions alerts, adverse media, or failure to maintain current beneficial ownership records.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1981-82 (Cook Islands), as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2008-09; ss. 4-18 (Incorporation and Effect of Articles), s. 33 (Registered Office), s. 44 (Directors), s. 61 (Secretary), and s. 176 (Tax Exemption for Non-Resident-Owned International Companies); applicable within the unitary legal framework of the Realm of New Zealand
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) - Registry Division, Companies Office, Rarotonga
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation together with Form FSC-IC-1 (Application for Incorporation of an International Company), executed by the incorporator and lodged with the Registrar of International Companies
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for an International Company; the Company must issue at least one share of any denomination, commonly USD 1.00 or NZD 1.00; no escrow account, capitalisation deposit, or capital duty is required under the International Companies Act
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] INTERNATIONAL COMPANY (THE 'COMPANY'), ADOPTED ON [DATE] AT [PLACE] OR BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT OF THE SOLE FIRST DIRECTOR.

1. INCORPORATION ADOPTION: RESOLVED that the incorporation of the Company as an international company limited by shares under the International Companies Act 1981-82 (Cook Islands) (the 'Act'), with registration number [NUMBER] and registered office at the office of [REGISTERED AGENT NAME], licensed registered agent, Rarotonga, Cook Islands, be and is hereby ratified and adopted.

2. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: RESOLVED that the authorised share capital of the Company be and is hereby fixed at USD 100,000 divided into 100,000 ordinary shares of USD 1.00 each; that the subscription of one (1) ordinary share of USD 1.00 by [SUBSCRIBER NAME] (the 'Initial Shareholder') be and is hereby approved; that the liability of the Initial Shareholder is limited to the amount unpaid on such share; and that share certificate number 1 be issued to the Initial Shareholder and entered in the register of shareholders.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE AND REGISTERED AGENT: RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be established at [REGISTERED AGENT ADDRESS], Rarotonga, Cook Islands, being the office of [REGISTERED AGENT NAME], a registered agent licensed by the Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission; that such registered agent be and is hereby appointed as the agent of the Company for service of process; and that the directors be authorised to change the registered office or registered agent only by further board resolution filed with the Registrar.

4. OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: RESOLVED that [DIRECTOR NAME] be and is hereby appointed as the first director of the Company to hold office until the first annual general meeting of shareholders or until earlier removal or retirement; that [SECRETARY NAME] be and is hereby appointed as secretary of the Company; and that each such officer consents to act and that their appointment be recorded in the register of directors and officers.

5. OPENING OF BANK ACCOUNTS AND COMMERCIAL AUTHORISATIONS: RESOLVED that the bankers of the Company be and are hereby designated as [BANK NAME]; that the directors be and are hereby authorised, jointly or severally, to open, operate, and close bank and custody accounts, to sign cheques and electronic payment instructions, to appoint payment gateway providers, and to execute agreements with Apple App Store, Google Play Store, and Stripe for the commercial operation of the Company's vertical micro-drama streaming application and global content distribution.

6. GENERAL AUTHORITY: RESOLVED that the directors be and are hereby authorised to do all acts, execute all documents, and take all steps as they may consider necessary or desirable to give full effect to the foregoing resolutions, including completing Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission annual return registrations, foreign qualification filings in New Zealand, and such other registrations as may be required in target markets in which the Company carries on business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) - Registry Division, via a licensed Cook Islands registered agent online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request on Form FSC-IC-2 to the Registrar of International Companies, proposing up to three names in order of priority. Each proposed name must end with 'International Company', the suffix 'IC', or 'Limited'/'Ltd', must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name, and must not contravene the prohibited names provisions of the Act. Upon approval, the name is reserved for a period of thirty (30) days.
required_dossiers: Form FSC-IC-2 (Name Reservation Request)
Due diligence name search report
Letter of engagement from a licensed Cook Islands registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, the applicant may file an amended reservation request with alternative names within the reservation period; the applicant may also request the Registrar to state written reasons and may apply for judicial review before the High Court of the Cook Islands.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator and licensed registered agent (pre-filing stage)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporator executes the Articles of Incorporation in the prescribed form, setting out the company name, statement of purpose, share capital structure, and the election to be registered as an international company. The registered agent countersigns its consent to act. Signatures of non-resident subscribers must be notarised or witnessed by a bank or counsel, and all identity documents must be certified as true copies.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation
Consent of Registered Agent
Notarised or certified passport copies of the incorporator and first director
Proof of residential address for the incorporator and first director
Bank reference letter for each subscriber and director
AML/KYC questionnaire completed for each beneficial owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FSC notifies a defect in the constitutional instrument, the registered agent will procure a corrective instrument from the incorporator and resubmit within fourteen (14) days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) - Registrar of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent lodges the executed Articles of Incorporation with Form FSC-IC-1 and the prescribed filing fee of USD 250 by e-filing or physical lodgement at the FSC Registry. The Registrar examines the application for compliance with the Act; upon satisfaction, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation dated and signed. The Company is constituted on the date of the certificate, which is the incorporation date.
required_dossiers: Form FSC-IC-1 (Application for Incorporation of an International Company)
Executed Articles of Incorporation
Proof of payment of the USD 250 state filing fee
Consent of Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the registered agent has thirty (30) days to supply supplementary information under section 13 of the Act; if the Registrar refuses incorporation, the applicant may appeal to the Minister responsible for financial supervision and thereafter to the High Court of the Cook Islands.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirmation of Registered Office and Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Registered Agent under the supervision of the Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following incorporation, the registered agent files Form FSC-IC-4 (Notice of Registered Office) to confirm the registered office address in the Cook Islands, being the licensed office of the registered agent, and to confirm the appointment of such agent. The registered office must be maintained continuously and be open during normal business hours for service of process and inspection.
required_dossiers: Form FSC-IC-4 (Notice of Registered Office)
Registered Agent Agreement
Board Resolution appointing the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In the event of a non-compliant filing, the FSC will notify the registered agent, who must file a corrective notice within five (5) business days; late filing penalties may be waived upon written request demonstrating reasonable cause.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Constitutive Board Meeting and Adoption of Corporate Governance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Company (internal corporate organ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The first director(s) hold the constitutive board meeting or adopt written resolutions in lieu of a meeting, adopting the First Board Resolution which covers: (i) ratification of incorporation; (ii) approval of share capital subscription; (iii) adoption of the registered office and appointment of the registered agent; (iv) appointment of the first director and secretary; and (v) opening of bank accounts and authorisation of platform agreements. The secretary then opens and maintains the statutory registers of shareholders, directors, and charges.
required_dossiers: First Board Meeting Minutes or Written Resolutions
Share certificates issued to the initial shareholder
Statutory registers (shareholders, directors, and charges)
Signed consents to act from each appointed officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any defect in the governance record is curable by a confirming board resolution and an amended entry in the company's statutory records; no court procedure is required for purely internal governance corrections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Annual Compliance and Platform Onboarding Notifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) for annual return; Apple Developer Program, Google Play Console, and Stripe as commercial platform onboarding authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent files the annual return on the anniversary of incorporation, confirms the particulars on the register, and pays the annual government fee of USD 300. No local tax registration is required by reason of the tax-exempt status of a non-resident-owned international company. For the vertical micro-drama streaming business, the Company completes platform accreditations in its own legal name, including Apple Developer Program enrolment, Google Play Console verification, and Stripe business verification, together with the publication of a privacy policy and platform content rating self-classification.
required_dossiers: FSC Annual Return
Declaration of non-resident ownership and tax-exempt status
Payment receipt for the FSC annual government fee
Apple Developer Program and Google Play Console verification documents
Stripe business verification documents and beneficial ownership declaration
Privacy policy and app privacy label disclosures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late filing of the annual return attracts a penalty of USD 200; an extension or waiver may be requested in writing to the FSC within thirty (30) days of the due date, which is generally granted on a showing of reasonable cause.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no industrial or manufacturing licensing board has authority over ISIC 5911 cloud-based digital content production; in the Cook Islands, no industrial licence applies to vertical micro-drama production and over-the-top streaming distribution by an International Company
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no statutory operating permit is required for a digital-only vertical micro-drama production and distribution company under the International Companies Act 1981-82 or any Cook Islands media licensing law; Apple Developer Program membership, Google Play Console registration, and Stripe account verification are voluntary commercial onboarding prerequisites rather than statutory licences

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Triggered - Class 5 Exempt Determination: the Company conducts no physical production, no studio construction, no manufacturing plant, and no waste-generating operation within the Cook Islands; the business is wholly cloud-based content production and global streaming distribution, so no Environmental Impact Assessment report or project registration is required under the Environment Act 2003
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero on-shore wastewater discharge and zero VOC emissions; all processing and hosting are performed in leased cloud data centres outside the Cook Islands, which must comply with the data centre operator's environmental and energy-efficiency standards (e.g., ISO 14001 or the EU Code of Conduct for Energy Efficiency); any electronic waste arising from future local office equipment, if a physical office is established, must be handled in accordance with the Environment Act 2003 and applicable transboundary e-waste transport rules, with nil tolerance for unauthorised dumping or open burning

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable on-shore for a remote digital workforce with no physical premises. Should the Company later establish a representative office in Rarotonga, the following clearances become mandatory: (i) fire safety clearance from the Cook Islands Fire Service, including means-of-escape certification and fire protection system inspection; (ii) building occupancy and structural load clearance from the Cook Islands Ministry of Infrastructure and Planning; (iii) workplace safety clearance and occupational registration under applicable Cook Islands workplace health and safety legislation once employees are engaged; and (iv) a trade licence from the Cook Islands Business Trade Licensing Authority if any physical commercial activity is conducted locally.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department of New Zealand (Te Tari Tāke) – operational online portal 'myIR' (https://www.ird.govt.nz)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity conducting taxable activities in New Zealand (including a non-resident company carrying on business through a fixed establishment or deriving New Zealand-sourced income) must register for a New Zealand IRD number (tax file number). For GST purposes, non-resident businesses may register for GST if they supply goods or services in New Zealand. Registration is effected by filing the prescribed application with Inland Revenue via myIR or paper form IR742; for GST registration, Form IR322 may be used for non-residents. The application requires the entity's legal name, jurisdictional place of incorporation, registered office and agent particulars in New Zealand, intended business activities, and estimated turnover. The IRD number is issued upon successful validation; GST registration takes effect from the date specified in the application or the date liability arises, and a GST registration number is issued separately. Non-resident companies becoming liable to income tax in New Zealand should also complete company IRD registration and may need to appoint a New Zealand agent for service of process.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A foreign company not managed and controlled in New Zealand is generally treated as non-resident for New Zealand income tax purposes, subject to New Zealand tax only on New Zealand-sourced income and certain controlled foreign company (CFC) attribution rules under the Income Tax Act 2007. No general check-the-box election akin to the US regime exists; however, an entity may make elections regarding the recognition of losses under the CFC rules, the deemed tax credit election for foreign imputation credits, and residency alignment elections under dual-resident company provisions. Hybrid mismatch rules under Subpart FH of the Income Tax Act 2007 may require the New Zealand entity or its investors to make adjustments where an offshore entity is treated as transparent in one jurisdiction and opaque in another; the statutory mechanism includes the requirement to file disclosure forms (IR547) and to apply the primary and defensive hybrid mismatch rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (Goods and Services Tax) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in New Zealand in any 12-month period, or from the first day a person intends to make taxable supplies in New Zealand and reasonably expects to exceed NZD 60,000 in the ensuing 12 months; non-resident suppliers of 'remote services' to New Zealand consumers must register once annual supplies exceed NZD 60,000 (same threshold), with an optional low-value goods registration threshold of NZD 60,000 for goods supplied to New Zealand consumers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not currently mandate a real-time electronic invoicing or fiscal clearance regime for GST purposes. A business-to-business (B2B) e-invoicing framework based on the Peppol standard is voluntary and operated through accredited access points. GST-registered persons must issue a tax invoice within 28 days of the time of supply and must retain sufficient electronic records; non-resident suppliers registered under the GST remote services regime may issue simplified tax invoices. There is no government API-based real-time clearance, digital stamping, or pre-clearance authorisation for invoices, although Inland Revenue may require electronic lodgement of GST returns via myIR or gateway software.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, a GST-registered person may zero-rate supplies of goods that are exported from New Zealand by the supplier, or supplied for shipping outside New Zealand, provided the goods are exported as part of a supply to a non-resident recipient and documentary evidence of export is retained. Services supplied to non-resident persons who are outside New Zealand when the services are performed are generally zero-rated as 'remote services', unless the services are supplied to a New Zealand resident or the services are supplied in connection with land or moveable property situated in New Zealand. Zero-rating also applies to the supply of a going concern, ongoing services to international airlines, and certain internationally connected transactions. The supplier must obtain and retain proof of export and evidence that the recipient is a non-resident; the zero-rating claim can be allocated to the relevant GST return period.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (New Zealand Customs Service – Export Declaration / Export Entry via TSW system)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing shipment of goods from New Zealand
Inward Remittance Certificate or certificate of foreign exchange receipt evidencing payment from the non-resident recipient
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is subject to Inland Revenue audit scrutiny, requiring contemporaneous documentary evidence that the goods have been physically exported within a reasonable time (normally within 28 days of supply, or within 60 days where supply is arranged by the recipient) and that the supply was made to a non-resident. Where the statutory conditions are not satisfied, GST is payable at the standard 15% rate and penalties and interest may be imposed under the Tax Administration Act 1994: late payment penalties of 1% per month on unpaid amounts plus imputed interest of approximately 9.23% (updated quarterly), shortfall penalties ranging from 20% (not taking reasonable care) to 150% (fraud or evasion), and a criminal fine up to NZD 50,000 for evading GST. A clawback may be assessed by amending the relevant GST return within the four-year statutory assessment period, or indefinitely in cases of fraud or gross negligence; the Commissioner may also issue an assessment for unpaid GST and tax shortfall penalties with retrospective effect to the time of supply.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 2021; foreign exchange administration is decentralized without a dedicated FX control bureau, while registered banks and licensed financial service providers are supervised primarily by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand for prudential conduct and by the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) for market conduct and disclosure obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains full and unrestricted convertibility of the New Zealand Dollar (NZD) on both current and capital account dimensions, with no applicable exchange control legislation since the revocation of the Foreign Exchange Control Regulations in 1984. Profit remittance, dividend distribution, and capital repatriation for a New Zealand International Company are freely permissible without central bank approval, subject only to ordinary company law solvency tests and any applicable non-resident withholding tax or thin capitalization rules under the Income Tax Act 2007. The non-resident-owned entity is not subject to any currency conversion mandate, and the NZD is freely tradeable in both onshore and offshore markets. Limitations on foreign investment arise solely under the Overseas Investment Act 2005 for transactions involving 'sensitive land' or 'significant business assets' (the latter only relevant where the entity acquires such assets, not for the entity's basic establishment or ongoing foreign shareholder funding).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export proceeds surrender regime. No mandatory conversion ratio, no repatriation timeline, and no obligation to sell foreign currency earned from digital content distribution, licensing, or in-app purchase settlement into NZD. Exporters and digital-service sellers, including the vertical micro-drama streaming operator, may freely retain foreign currency earnings in offshore nostro accounts or onshore foreign-currency-denominated accounts at registered banks. The only compliance burden is statistical: registered banks must report cross-border transactions to the Reserve Bank of New Zealand and Statistics New Zealand under the Balance of Payments and International Investment Position reporting framework; however, the entity itself has no direct filing duty unless it qualifies as a reporting enterprise under the Financial Reporting Act 2013.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: High with legal constraints. Registered non-bank financial institutions operating as electronic money institutions (EMIs) in New Zealand, including Wise (formerly TransferWise) NZ, Airwallex NZ, OFX, and Ebury, offer multi-currency IBAN wallets and rapid settlement with valid Financial Service Provider (FSP) registration under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 and as reporting entities under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. These EMIs provide viable treasury rails for receiving Apple IAP, Google Play Billing, and Stripe settlement proceeds in USD, EUR, AUD, and GBP, with auto-conversion into NZD or USD for onward disbursement. Legal constraints: (1) an offshore EMI without New Zealand registration cannot lawfully provide cross-border payment services to a New Zealand-based company, and the entity must ensure the EMI holds a valid FSP license and an agent/trustee arrangement if it is a foreign EEA/UK EMI passporting under NZ's Part 6 inbound registration; (2) EMIs are not eligible to provide credit facilities or hold term deposit liquidity, and their deposits are not guaranteed under the RBNZ depositor compensation scheme; (3) for LG round trip capital escrow, a licensed tier-1 commercial bank, not an EMI, must be the primary custodian of share capital, while an EMI may operate as a sub-account for operational clearing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory mandate requiring directors to appear physically in New Zealand; however, tier-1 registered banks uniformly require either (a) an in-person or secure video conference interview with all signatories and 25% or greater beneficial owners, or (b) acceptance of a 'Remote Opening' package comprising notarized certified copies of passports, proof of address, and a certified board resolution, with subsequent verification via video call. Because the target entity is a Tax-Exempt Zone International Company with non-resident ownership and no statutory operating license, most banks will classify the onboarding as 'standard risk' but will still require: (i) a New Zealand registered office address, (ii) a physical service itinerary for the first 12 months of operation (e.g., office space, independent local contractor agreement), (iii) a local AML/CFT designated agent if the company obtains an FSP registration, and (iv) at least one senior manager who can attend interviews during local business hours (UTC+12). Directors who are politically exposed persons or who reside in FATF grey-listed jurisdictions (e.g., Barbados, Jamaica, Morocco, Philippines, Uganda) will trigger an Enhanced Due Diligence interview that generally requires physical presence at a New Zealand embassy or a scheduled bank video conference with a compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident-owned International Company with no local tax registration and no physical operating assets, perceived as a pure shell/anonymity vehicle
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Certificate of Incorporation and Constitution of the International Company; (2) Register of directors and shareholders with ultimate beneficial owner declaration (Form CA02); (3) Tax exemption certificate or off-shore company tax status confirmation issued by the Inland Revenue Department (IRD); (4) Substance pack: office lease or registered agent agreement, local telephone/business correspondence, and a board resolution confirming treasury and payment operations are managed from New Zealand; (5) 12-month business plan and minimum projected revenue to evidence economic activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound shareholder capital injection from a related entity domiciled in a restricted jurisdiction (e.g., PRC parent) without clear equity documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Fully executed share subscription agreement and board resolution approving issuance of shares; (2) HKMA/SAFE outbound investment approval certificate (including SAFE filing for FDI) where applicable; (3) Source-of-wealth statement covering shareholder's corporate bank statement and financial statements for the last 2 years; (4) Bank reference letter from the remitting bank confirming KYC was completed; (5) Written confirmation that proceeds are used exclusively for app development, production, and global distribution working capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Scattered app store proceeds from multiple jurisdictions (Apple IAP, Google Play Billing, Stripe) causing disproportionate transaction pattern versus invoiced revenue
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) App store payout statements from Apple, Google, and Stripe with waterfall royalty calculations; (2) Concise revenue recognition policy and management accounts, or board-pack brief; (3) Reconciliation file linking gross billed revenue, platform commissions, consumer tax (VAT/GST) withholdings, and net settlement; (4) Signed distribution agreements with OTT partners and regional licensing agents; (5) Open letter from external accountant (CPA) confirming refund and chargeback accounting treatment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound disbursements to high-risk production and subcontractor countries (e.g., Indonesia, Philippines, Kenya, India) for dubbing, subtitling, or localized production teams
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Full vendor contracts and non-disclosure agreements; (2) Invoices against services rendered with employment/contractor verification; (3) Beneficial ownership declaration of vendor bank receiving funds; (4) Evidence of local content production approval or co-production certificate if required; (5) Escrow or milestone payment schedule in the master services agreement; (6) Negative-media search for each vendor and a third-party due diligence report from a firm such as Dow Jones or Thomson Reuters.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing is executed via SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident shareholder's bank to the New Zealand International Company's Operational NZD or multi-currency account with a tier-1 NZ bank. No mandatory purpose code regime exists, but the remittance reference field must clearly identify the transaction as 'Share Subscription – APIC (Additional Paid-In Capital)' with a covering note stating the Companies Office file number and the relevant board resolution date. Remittance data should include the Overseas Investment Act 2005 exemption status (no consent required for a new startup entity not acquiring sensitive assets) and a statement that the funds constitute equity injection, not intercompany debt. The receiving bank will apply a standard 'non-resident company – shareholder equity' reason code for BOP statistical purposes. Upon confirmation of settlement, the company must (i) update the New Zealand Companies Office share register within 20 working days, (ii) file an annual return, and (iii) for tax-exempt International Companies, maintain the exemption certificate file. If the inbound transfer exceeds NZD 50,000, the bank will require the evidentiary dossier previously enumerated (source of funds, subscription agreement, SAFE approval) prior to crediting, with a typical same-day or next-business-day availability.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail: SWIFT MT103 (single payment) via the onshore bank's direct clearing network for content licensing fees, production services, IP royalties, and overseas contractor wages. For high-value production financing milestones (above USD 250,000) where an irrevocable payment undertaking is contractually required, a standard Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) with a confirmed advising bank can be established, but this is atypical for vertical micro-drama working capital cycles in which production-to-cash is rapid. App store settlement is handled through Apple's and Google's mass-payment systems, with funds remitted in USD, EUR, or NZD via wire transfers to the company's NZD account; for jurisdictions without direct settlement (e.g., incountry OTT partners), use SWIFT MT103 with OTT's designated account. All outbound disbursements should be made to accounts in the name of the contracted vendor (no third-party beneficiaries) and include commercial invoice numbers in the SWIFT field 72/77 to facilitate bank reconciliation. The banks in New Zealand currently support Fast Payment (Domestic Clearing) for local disbursements, but international outbound payments remain reliant on the SWIFT network with an expected value date of T+1 to T+3 depending on the destination. Treasury should maintain USD, EUR, and AUD clearing accounts at the primary bank to reduce conversion spreads and to filter app store settlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forwards (plain vanilla deliverable forward contracts up to 24 months by maturity) – permitted with all tier-1 NZ registered bank counterparties for USD/NZD, AUD/NZD, EUR/NZD, GBP/NZD and JPY/NZD

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) – permitted via NZ and international third-party counterparties for restricted currencies (CNY offshore, THB, PHP, IDR, VND, MYR, KRW, INR) with standard net-cash settled NDF conventions in USD

Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS) – permitted for converting long-term foreign-currency (especially USD) app store receivable streams into NZD liabilities, or for hedging an AUD- or USD-denominated production financing facility; requires a registered NZ financial service provider

FX options (European-style call/put on spot and forwards) – permitted, but usually only utilized for highly committed production capex and are offered by the top four banks under standard ISDA documentation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation & Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one calendar month after the annual return date, being the anniversary of the date of incorporation; the return period is the preceding 12 months ending the day before the annual return date. The Companies Office applies a 20-working-day administrative grace period before assessing late filing penalties.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 200; failure to comply with a Registrar default notice requiring filing within 20 working days is an offence punishable by fines up to NZD 10,000 for the company and each director; continued default enables Registrar-initiated removal from the Register (strike-off) and dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited annual financial statements (filing mandatory only for 'large' companies or where shareholders holding at least 5% of voting rights have resolved to require an audit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation & Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For large companies, within 20 working days of the date the financial statements are completed and signed, which date must be not later than 5 months after the balance date; small exempt companies have no filing deadline but must prepare financial statements within 5 months of balance date when an audit is required.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors commit an offence and are liable on conviction to fines up to NZD 10,000; the Registrar may issue a notice requiring delivery and, on default, initiate removal (strike-off) proceedings against the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST returns and payment (compulsory registration once annual taxable turnover exceeds NZD 60,000; recurring filing obligation for the streaming app revenue model)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the 28th day of the month following the end of each taxable period; filing frequency is monthly, two-monthly, six-monthly, or annual depending on turnover and IRD approval.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 250 per return plus NZD 50 for each additional month (capped at NZD 1,000 per return); use-of-money interest applies to unpaid GST; failure to remit can trigger the director penalty notice regime making directors personally liable.
